meta.name: Red Eye Cafe
meta.about: Slinging great food and drinks since 2012, Red Eye Cafe has led the way for the growing Walnut Street food and coffee scene. Often imitated but never duplicated, Red Eye stays true to its mission to deliver quality stuff, at a good price, without all the fluff.
meta.priceNote: Prices are in-store base prices. Items marked source "official-pdf" come directly from Red Eye's own printed menus (Menu 12.05.25, downloaded from redeyenj.com). Items marked "grubhub-derived" exist only on the delivery platforms; their prices were converted back to in-store base by removing the platform markup, which was verified to be exactly 10% across dozens of overlapping items (e.g. Elvis $7.70 on Grubhub vs. $7 on the printed menu, Salmon BLT $17.60 vs. $16). Derived prices may be off by a cent from the true register price. Coffee prices shown are the 12 oz price; larger sizes are listed in the item description. Delivery-platform prices (Grubhub, DoorDash, Uber Eats, MenuPix) run roughly 10% higher than these.
meta.popularNote: The "Popular" tag reflects the union of Grubhub "Best Seller" badges, DoorDash Featured/Most Liked items, and MenuPix "Popular Menu Items".
gaps: No kids' menu appears on the official site or on any delivery platform.
No bakery/pastry list is published anywhere; Grubhub reviewers note bakery goods must be added by calling the cafe directly and paying separately.
The 20 oz Matcha Latte price is physically cut off in the official PDF (reads "6."); Grubhub implies roughly $6.57 in-store, so it is left out rather than guessed.
Soup of the day rotates daily and is not published; the menu says to call.
Uber Eats is behind a Cloudflare bot check and could not be read; Grubhub and DoorDash carry the same nine categories, so nothing appears to be missing.
The MenuPix listing links an outdated website (drinkredeyes.com) and shows delivery-platform prices, so it was used only for cross-checking popular items.
"Single-Use Items" ($0.00 utensil opt-in) appears on Grubhub in every category and was intentionally excluded.
Specials rotate; the five listed were live on Grubhub at the time of research.
